title: The Thinking Behind the Prompt: Evidence From Collaborative Student Problem Solving With Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: ABSTRACT Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools are permeating education but whether cognitive dispositions moderate their benefits remains unclear. In the present work, we examined whether Cognitive Reflection and Intolerance of Uncertainty moderate the relationship between prior GenAI experience and collaborative task effectiveness. Specifically, secondary ( n = 114) and tertiary ( n = 57) students, distributed across groups, completed a mystery‐solving task with unrestricted access to a GenAI tool of their choice. Person‐centred analysis identified no cognitive‐attitudinal profiles as the solution collapsed onto three groups defined by the Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) score. In exploratory comparisons, the High‐CRT group reported greater post‐task prompting self‐efficacy than the Low‐CRT group, despite no detectable difference in performance. Cognitive reflection did not moderate the experience‐effectiveness link at the group level and uncertainty intolerance did not predict AI reliance behaviours. Therefore, cognitive dispositions appear to relate more closely to the subjective experience of working with AI than to objective task outcomes.
